products.title: Alyssum
products.description: Sweet alyssum is a delicate annual ground cover producing masses of tiny, honey-scented white or pink flowers. Native to the Mediterranean, it blooms prolifically and attracts beneficial insects like bees and butterflies.

symbolism.origin: Named 'sweet alyssum' for its honey-like fragrance; Victorians saw its modest, low-growing form as representing worth that surpasses outward appearance.

products.title: Alstroemeria
products.description: Also called Peruvian Lily or Lily of the Incas, alstroemeria produces vibrant, long-lasting blooms with characteristic streaked inner petals. Native to South America, it symbolizes friendship and devotion.

symbolism.origin: The leaves twist as they grow outward, symbolizing the trials, turns, and steadfast support found in a true friendship.

products.title: Azelea
products.description: Azalea is a flowering shrub prized for its spectacular spring display of large, showy blooms. It prefers acidic soil and partial shade, and is a staple of cottage and Japanese-style gardens.

symbolism.origin: Azaleas are short-lived and sensitive to excess water, symbolizing fragility and restraint.

products.title: Balsam
products.description: Garden balsam (Impatiens balsamina) is an old-fashioned annual with cup-shaped, camellia-like flowers nestled among lance-shaped leaves. It thrives in warm, humid conditions and is beloved for its ease of care.

symbolism.origin: Ripe seed pods burst open at the slightest touch, giving rise to the genus name Impatiens and a Victorian symbol of restless ardor.

products.title: Begonia
products.description: Begonias are versatile flowering plants prized for their colorful blooms and attractive foliage. Available in hundreds of varieties, they are ideal for shade gardens, hanging baskets, and containers, blooming from spring to frost.

symbolism.origin: Named after Michel Bégon; its sound-alike phrase “be gone” suggested caution.

products.title: Calendula
products.description: Calendula, or pot marigold, is a bright annual with cheerful orange and yellow daisy-like flowers. Its petals are edible and have been used medicinally since ancient times for their anti-inflammatory and skin-healing properties.

symbolism.origin: Flowers open and close faithfully with the sun each day; Victorians associated this constancy with grief borne quietly and sacred affection.

products.title: California Poppy
products.description: The California poppy is the state flower of California, producing silky, cup-shaped blooms in shades of orange, yellow, and cream. It is drought-tolerant, self-seeding, and thrives in poor, well-drained soils.

symbolism.origin: Its brilliant golden petals, glowing like sunlight across the hills, evoked visions of wealth and the promise of good fortune.

products.title: Calla Lily
products.description: Calla lily (Zantedeschia) is renowned for its elegant, trumpet-shaped spathe and glossy arrow-shaped leaves. A favorite in bridal bouquets and ornamental gardens, it conveys purity and magnificent beauty.

symbolism.origin: Its pure white spathe and flawless, sculpted form made it a symbol of regal magnificence in Victorian parlors and bridal ceremonies.

products.title: Carnation
products.description: Carnations (Dianthus caryophyllus) are among the oldest cultivated flowers, prized for their spicy, clove-like fragrance and ruffled, fringed petals. They symbolize love and fascination and come in virtually every color.

symbolism.origin: Linked to the Virgin Mary’s tears at Christ’s crucifixion.

products.title: Chrysanthemum
products.description: Chrysanthemums, or mums, are the quintessential autumn flower, producing dense pompom or daisy-like blooms in a vast spectrum of colors. In East Asian cultures they symbolize longevity and rejuvenation.

symbolism.origin: Commonly used in European funerals and All Souls’ Day rituals.

products.title: Dahlia
products.description: Dahlias are tuberous perennials native to Mexico and Central America, producing showy blooms in an astonishing variety of forms and colors from midsummer until frost. They were once prized as a food source by the Aztecs.

symbolism.origin: Long-lasting blooms made it a Victorian wedding symbol.

products.title: Daffodil
products.description: Daffodils (Narcissus) are iconic spring bulbs bearing cheerful yellow or white trumpet-shaped flowers. They are among the first flowers to bloom after winter and are toxic to most animals, deterring pests naturally.

symbolism.origin: From the myth of Narcissus falling in love with his reflection.

products.title: Daisy
products.description: The classic garden daisy features pristine white ray petals surrounding a bright yellow disc center. Simple and cheerful, it has appeared in mythology and literature across cultures as a symbol of innocence and new beginnings.

symbolism.origin: Appears in Norse, Celtic, and Roman mythology as a symbol of innocence.

products.title: Damask Rose
products.description: The Damask rose (Rosa damascena) is a legendary ancient rose originating in the Middle East, famed for its intensely rich fragrance. It is the primary source of rose water and rose attar used in perfumery worldwide.

symbolism.origin: Brought to Europe by Crusaders from Damascus; its intoxicating fragrance and layered petals became synonymous with timeless, devoted love.

products.title: Delphinium (Larkspur)
products.description: Delphiniums, also known as larkspur, produce magnificent tall spikes densely packed with spurred flowers in deep blues, purples, and whites. They are a majestic presence in cottage gardens and cutting gardens alike.

symbolism.origin: Named for a lark’s foot; associated with lightness.

products.title: Dianthus
products.description: Dianthus, commonly called pinks, are fragrant perennial or annual flowers with fringed, tooth-edged petals in shades of pink, red, and white. The name means "flower of the gods" in Greek.

symbolism.origin: The name means 'flower of the gods' in Greek; Victorians used it to express a love that was both divine and boldly declared.

products.title: Geranium
products.description: Garden geraniums (Pelargonium) are among the most popular container and bedding plants worldwide, valued for their bright flower clusters, attractive leaves, and robust nature. They thrive in sunny spots with well-drained soil.

symbolism.origin: The showy scarlet blooms were considered deceptively simple; Victorians used it to gently signal folly or a lack of depth.

products.title: Godetia
products.description: Godetia (Clarkia amoena), also known as Farewell-to-Spring, is a Western North American wildflower producing large, silky, cup-shaped blooms in shades of pink, red, lavender, and white. It prefers cool weather.

symbolism.origin: Called Farewell-to-Spring for its late blooming; its vivid, fleeting flowers inspired a Victorian sense of being utterly captivated.

products.title: Gladiolus
products.description: Gladiolus produces dramatic tall spikes of large, funnel-shaped flowers in nearly every color. Originally from South Africa, the corms are planted in spring for summer blooms that are spectacular as cut flowers.

symbolism.origin: From *gladius*, Latin for sword.

products.title: Hollyhock
products.description: Hollyhocks are stately biennials or perennials that send up towering spikes of large, single or double flowers in a wide range of colors. A cottage garden classic, they often self-seed freely along walls and fences.

symbolism.origin: Its towering spikes reaching skyward above garden walls inspired Victorians to see it as the emblem of lofty ambition and fertile abundance.

products.title: Hyacinth
products.description: Hyacinths are spring-blooming bulbs renowned for their intensely sweet, heady fragrance and dense racemes of small, star-shaped flowers. They are perfect for forcing indoors in winter for early color and scent.

symbolism.origin: From Apollo’s grief over Hyacinthus in Greek myth.

products.title: Iris
products.description: Irises are elegant perennials with distinctive sword-like foliage and intricate, bearded or beardless flowers. Named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow, they come in virtually every color and combination.

symbolism.origin: Symbol of victory in Egyptian and Frankish history.

products.title: Jasmine
products.description: Jasmine (Jasminum) is a climbing or shrubby plant producing clusters of small, intensely fragrant white or yellow flowers. Widely used in garlands, tea, and perfumery across Asia, it is a symbol of amiability and grace.

symbolism.origin: Celebratory flower in many Asian cultures.

products.title: Lavender
products.description: Lavender is an aromatic Mediterranean shrub producing spikes of small purple flowers beloved by pollinators. Its dried flowers and essential oil are used extensively in aromatherapy, cosmetics, and culinary applications.

symbolism.origin: Linked to venomous snakes and Cleopatra’s legend.

products.title: Lilac
products.description: Lilacs are deciduous shrubs or small trees that produce spectacular clusters of intensely fragrant flowers in spring. Hardy and long-lived, they are a cherished feature of temperate gardens and a symbol of first love.

symbolism.origin: Greek myth of Pan and Syringa.

products.title: Marigold
products.description: Marigolds are cheerful, sun-loving annuals producing bold pompom flowers in shades of orange, yellow, and gold. Easy to grow and prolific, they are widely used as companion plants to deter garden pests.

symbolism.origin: Used in Day of the Dead rituals and Aztec lore.

products.title: Morning Glory
products.description: Morning glories are fast-growing annual vines producing a profusion of trumpet-shaped flowers that open fresh each morning. Their vibrant blooms in blue, purple, pink, and white make them ideal for fences and trellises.

symbolism.origin: Flowers bloom brilliantly each morning only to close by afternoon; Victorians read this as a token of fleeting affection and love in vain.

products.title: Pansy
products.description: Pansies are charming cool-weather annuals with distinctive "face" markings on their velvety petals. Available in an extraordinary range of colors and bi-colors, they are a beloved staple of spring and autumn gardens.

symbolism.origin: From the French *pensée*, meaning thought.

products.title: Peony
products.description: Peonies are long-lived herbaceous perennials producing enormous, luxuriously fragrant blooms in shades of white, pink, and red. Among the most cherished of all garden flowers, they can live and bloom for over a century.

symbolism.origin: Greek nymphs hid by transforming into peonies.

products.title: Periwinkle
products.description: Periwinkle (Vinca) is a low-maintenance evergreen ground cover or trailing plant with glossy dark green leaves and cheerful five-petaled flowers in blue, violet, or white. It thrives in sun or shade with minimal care.

symbolism.origin: Evergreen and enduring, its small persistent flowers were treasured by Victorians as an emblem of cherished memories and tender recollection.

products.title: Phlox
products.description: Phlox is a North American native producing masses of star-shaped, fragrant flowers in a wide range of colors. Garden phlox is a cottage garden staple, while creeping phlox creates a carpet of spring color.

symbolism.origin: Dense clusters of individual flowers growing as one mass symbolized hearts united and complete unanimity of feeling.

products.title: Pink Rose
products.description: The traditional Kashmiri pink rose is a heritage variety prized for its full, fragrant blooms in delicate shades of pink. Grown in the famous rose gardens of Kashmir, it is used for rose water and as an ornamental.

symbolism.origin: Long-standing symbol of love in myth and culture.

products.title: Stocks
products.description: Stocks (Matthiola incana) are old-fashioned annuals or biennials producing tall spikes of densely packed, intensely fragrant flowers in shades of pink, white, red, and purple. Their sweet scent fills gardens in spring.

symbolism.origin: Long-lasting blooms and an enduring sweet fragrance led Victorians to see it as a symbol of a life lived in contented, lasting beauty.

products.title: Sunflower
products.description: Sunflowers are iconic annual plants native to North America, growing tall with large, golden ray flowers surrounding a central disc. They track the sun when young and produce nutritious seeds loved by birds and humans.

symbolism.origin: Inca gold symbolism misled Spanish explorers.

products.title: Sweet William
products.description: Sweet William (Dianthus barbatus) is a biennial or short-lived perennial producing dense, domed clusters of small, fragrant flowers in striking patterns of red, pink, white, and bicolors. A cottage garden classic.

symbolism.origin: Named for folkloric gallant young men.

products.title: Lily
products.description: True lilies (Lilium) are stately bulbous perennials producing large, often fragrant trumpet or turks cap flowers on tall stems. They come in a spectacular range of colors and are among the most beloved of all garden flowers.

symbolism.origin: Associated with the Virgin Mary in Christian art.

products.title: Tulip
products.description: Tulips are beloved spring-blooming bulbs native to Central Asia, producing elegant cup-shaped flowers in virtually every color of the spectrum. They were the subject of the famous 17th-century Dutch Tulipmania speculation.

symbolism.origin: Turkish legend of tragic devotion.
meanings: I declare my love for you

products.title: Verbena
products.description: Verbena is a sun-loving annual or perennial producing clusters of small, brightly colored flowers in shades of purple, pink, red, and white. Long-blooming and heat-tolerant, it is excellent for containers and hanging baskets.

symbolism.origin: Revered in Druidic and Roman sacred rites; Victorians regarded it as a charm of enchantment and a sincere plea for wishes to be granted.

products.title: Zinnia
products.description: Zinnias are vibrant, heat-loving annuals native to Mexico, producing bold daisy-like flowers in every color except blue. Easy to grow from seed and highly attractive to butterflies, they bloom continuously from summer to frost.

symbolism.origin: Easy growth and reseeding symbolized lasting bonds.

products.title: Amaryllis
products.description: Amaryllis (Hippeastrum) produces spectacular large, trumpet-shaped blooms on tall hollow stems, typically in red, white, or pink. Widely grown as a winter-flowering bulb indoors, it is prized for its bold and dramatic presence.

symbolism.origin: Victorians linked amaryllis to pride because of its tall stalks, bold blooms, and resilience to harsh conditions.

products.title: Anemone
products.description: Anemones are delicate, poppy-like flowers with silky petals in vivid shades of red, purple, pink, blue, and white, each with a striking dark center. They bloom in spring and are associated with Greek mythology and Aphrodite.

symbolism.origin: Greek mythology says anemones sprang from Aphrodite’s tears after the death of Adonis.

products.title: Apple Blossom
products.description: Apple blossoms are the delicate, five-petaled spring flowers of the apple tree. Pink-tinged in bud and white when open, they perfume orchards with a light, sweet fragrance and herald the arrival of spring.

symbolism.origin: From the myth of the Golden Apple of Discord and Paris choosing Aphrodite.

products.title: Asphodel
products.description: Asphodel is a tall Mediterranean perennial with strap-like leaves and elegant spikes of white or yellow star-shaped flowers. In Greek mythology, fields of asphodel were said to grow in the underworld.

symbolism.origin: In Greek myth, asphodels grew in the underworld and symbolized regret and limbo.
meanings: My regrets follow you to the grave

products.title: Aster
products.description: Asters are daisy-like perennials blooming in late summer and autumn in shades of purple, pink, blue, and white. They are an essential late-season source of nectar for pollinators and add color to the autumn garden.

symbolism.origin: Its slender petals surrounding a small center inspired delicacy and refinement.

products.title: Baby’s Breath
products.description: Baby's breath (Gypsophila) produces clouds of tiny, delicate white or pink flowers on wiry branching stems. A staple of the florist's art, it is used to add lightness and texture to bouquets and arrangements.

symbolism.origin: Named in the 19th century for its delicate scent and bridal-veil appearance.

products.title: Basil
products.description: Basil is a fragrant culinary herb with smooth, glossy leaves and small white or purple flowers. Native to tropical Asia and Africa, it is central to Mediterranean and Southeast Asian cuisines and has long medicinal uses.

symbolism.origin: Greeks likened basil leaves to the deadly basilisk, associating it with hatred.

products.title: Belladonna
products.description: Belladonna (Atropa belladonna), or deadly nightshade, is a poisonous perennial with dull green leaves, bell-shaped purple flowers, and shiny black berries. Historically used in medicine and as a cosmetic, it is extremely toxic.

symbolism.origin: A deadly poison historically used to kill, permanently silencing victims.

products.title: Bluebell
products.description: Bluebells are spring-flowering bulbs carpeting woodland floors with a haze of nodding, bell-shaped violet-blue flowers. Native to Western Europe, ancient bluebell woods are a celebrated natural spectacle in Britain.

symbolism.origin: The bowed, bell-shaped flowers suggest modesty and devotion.

products.title: Buttercup
products.description: Buttercups are cheerful perennial wildflowers with glossy, bright yellow petals that reflect light like lacquered gold. Common in meadows and pastures, they are familiar to generations of children for the buttercup chin test.

symbolism.origin: From a Victorian game testing buttercups under the chin for a golden glow.

products.title: Camellia
products.description: Camellias are elegant, evergreen shrubs producing exquisite rose-like flowers in shades of red, pink, and white during winter and early spring. Native to East Asia, they are prized as ornamentals and for tea production.

symbolism.origin: Popularized by Dumas’ novel *La dame aux camélias* about tragic longing.

products.title: Cattail
products.description: Cattails are tall aquatic or wetland plants with distinctive brown, cylindrical seed heads. They are among the most useful wild plants, with edible starch in the roots, and have been used for weaving and insulation.

symbolism.origin: Valued historically for food, fuel, insulation, and weaving.

products.title: Chamomile
products.description: Chamomile is a low-growing annual or perennial with feathery foliage and cheerful daisy-like flowers. Renowned since ancient Egypt for its calming, medicinal properties, chamomile tea is among the world's most popular herbal infusions.

symbolism.origin: Used since ancient Egypt for healing and renewal.

products.title: Clematis
products.description: Clematis is the queen of climbing plants, producing masses of showy four to eight petaled flowers in an enormous range of sizes, colors, and seasons. With the right variety, a garden wall can be clothed in bloom year-round.

symbolism.origin: Named for its clever ability to climb and adapt.

products.title: Clover
products.description: Clover is a low-growing legume with trifoliate leaves and rounded flower heads in white, pink, or red. Essential for soil fertility and beloved by bees, the rare four-leaf clover is a universal symbol of good luck.

symbolism.origin: Druidic and medieval folklore linked four-leaf clovers to fortune.

products.title: Columbine
products.description: Columbines (Aquilegia) are elegant perennials producing distinctive spurred flowers in a wide array of colors and bicolors. They attract hummingbirds and long-tongued bees and self-seed freely in the garden.

symbolism.origin: Linked to the jester Columbina and the bloom’s hat-like shape.

products.title: Cornflower
products.description: Cornflowers (Centaurea cyanus) are annual wildflowers producing intense sky-blue, purple, pink, or white flowers. Once common in European grain fields, they are now valued as cottage garden plants and cut flowers.

symbolism.origin: Folklore claimed its longevity predicted whether love would be returned.

products.title: Cowslip
products.description: Cowslips (Primula veris) are spring-flowering perennials with rosettes of crinkled leaves and clusters of nodding, fragrant yellow flowers. A traditional British wildflower, they thrive in meadows and chalk grasslands.

symbolism.origin: Legend says St. Peter’s dropped keys turned into cowslips.

products.title: Crocus
products.description: Crocuses are among the first flowers to emerge in late winter or early spring, often pushing through snow to reveal their cheerful cup-shaped blooms in purple, white, yellow, and striped varieties. The spice saffron comes from Crocus sativus.

symbolism.origin: One of the first flowers to bloom through snow.

products.title: Dandelion
products.description: Dandelions are resilient perennial wildflowers with toothed leaves, bright yellow flower heads, and spherical seed clocks. Every part is edible and medicinal, and their early nectar is vital for emerging spring pollinators.

symbolism.origin: Used for wishes and weather prediction.

products.title: Datura
products.description: Datura, or angel's trumpet, is a dramatic plant producing large, white funnel-shaped flowers that open at dusk and release a heady fragrance. All parts are highly toxic and have been used in shamanic rituals worldwide.

symbolism.origin: Beautiful but poisonous; linked to witchcraft lore.

products.title: Dogwood
products.description: Dogwood trees and shrubs are cherished ornamentals prized for their spectacular spring flowers, colorful autumn foliage, and decorative winter bark. The flowering dogwood is the state tree or flower of several US states.

symbolism.origin: Delicate blooms contrast with extremely strong wood.

products.title: Edelweiss
products.description: Edelweiss (Leontopodium alpinum) is an iconic Alpine flower with woolly white star-shaped bracts surrounding small yellow florets. Growing in high rocky terrain, it became a symbol of courage for those who dared to collect it.

symbolism.origin: Dangerous alpine harvesting symbolized bravery.

products.title: Eucalyptus
products.description: Eucalyptus trees are fast-growing Australian natives prized for their aromatic leaves, decorative peeling bark, and nectar-rich flowers. Eucalyptus oil is widely used medicinally, and the trees are vital habitat for koalas.

symbolism.origin: Used medicinally by Aboriginal peoples.

products.title: Fern
products.description: Ferns are ancient, non-flowering vascular plants with graceful, divided fronds. Among the oldest land plants on Earth, they thrive in shaded, moist environments and have long been associated with magic and the secret world of nature.

symbolism.origin: Water-repelling leaves inspired mystical associations.

products.title: Forget-me-not
products.description: Forget-me-nots are small, delicate spring flowers producing clusters of sky-blue blooms with yellow centers. They are among the most beloved of spring flowers and are a universal symbol of remembrance and undying love.

symbolism.origin: From a German folktale of lovers separated by a river.

products.title: Foxglove
products.description: Foxgloves (Digitalis) are tall biennials producing dramatic spikes of tubular, spotted flowers in shades of purple, pink, white, and yellow. The source of the heart medicine digitalis, they are beautiful but highly toxic.

symbolism.origin: Associated with fairies and dangerous enchantment.

products.title: Hawthorn
products.description: Hawthorn is a thorny deciduous shrub or small tree smothered in fragrant white or pink flowers in spring. Its red berries, called haws, are a vital winter food for birds, and it was considered sacred in ancient cultures.

symbolism.origin: Sacred wedding flower in ancient Greece.

products.title: Heather
products.description: Heather (Calluna vulgaris) is a low-growing evergreen shrub carpeting moorlands and heaths with a blaze of pink, purple, or white flowers in late summer. It is the signature plant of the Scottish Highlands.

symbolism.origin: Scottish legend of sorrow turning to fortune.

products.title: Hellebore
products.description: Hellebores are evergreen perennials producing nodding, cup-shaped flowers in winter and early spring, often in deep plum, burgundy, white, or spotted. Among the few plants to bloom in the depths of winter, they are prized shade garden plants.

symbolism.origin: Used medicinally and in Greek healing myths.

products.title: Hemlock
products.description: Poison hemlock (Conium maculatum) is a tall biennial with hollow, purple-blotched stems and flat-topped clusters of small white flowers. Notorious as the poison used to execute Socrates, it is extremely toxic.

symbolism.origin: Infamous poison used in the execution of Socrates.

products.title: Holly
products.description: Holly (Ilex) is an evergreen shrub or tree with glossy, spiny leaves and bright red berries. A symbol of Christmas and midwinter festivities, it has been used since ancient times in winter celebrations and for protection.

symbolism.origin: Used in European folklore for protection and divination.

products.title: Honeysuckle
products.description: Honeysuckle is a beloved climbing or bushy shrub producing sweetly fragrant tubular flowers in yellow, white, and pink that are irresistible to hummingbirds and moths. The sweet nectar can be sucked directly from the flowers.

symbolism.origin: Victorian belief that it caused dreams of true love.

products.title: Hydrangea
products.description: Hydrangeas are magnificent flowering shrubs producing enormous, dome-shaped or lacecap flower heads in shades of blue, pink, white, and purple. The flower color of some varieties is influenced by soil pH, turning blue in acidic soils.

symbolism.origin: Large blooms with few seeds suggested excess show.

products.title: Hyssop
products.description: Hyssop is a semi-evergreen aromatic herb with narrow leaves and spikes of small blue, violet, or pink flowers beloved by bees. Used since biblical times for purification, it has culinary and medicinal applications.

symbolism.origin: Used in ancient Greece and the Bible for purification.

products.title: Ivy
products.description: Ivy (Hedera) is a vigorous evergreen climbing or ground-covering plant with distinctive lobed leaves. Extraordinarily versatile and hardy, it clings to walls and trees with adhesive rootlets and provides vital winter shelter for wildlife.

symbolism.origin: Clings even after a tree dies, symbolizing devotion.

products.title: Lady Slipper
products.description: Lady slipper orchids (Cypripedium) are among the most spectacular of wildflowers, with their distinctive pouch-like lip in shades of pink, yellow, and white. Among the most difficult orchids to cultivate, they are protected in many countries.

symbolism.origin: Notoriously difficult and unpredictable to cultivate.

products.title: Larkspur
products.description: Larkspur (Delphinium consolida) is an annual producing tall, graceful spikes of spurred flowers in shades of blue, purple, pink, and white. A classic cottage garden and cutting garden annual, it dries beautifully for arrangements.

symbolism.origin: Named for a lark’s foot; associated with lightness.

products.title: Laurel
products.description: Bay laurel (Laurus nobilis) is an aromatic evergreen tree or shrub with glossy, leathery leaves used as a culinary herb. In ancient Greece and Rome, laurel wreaths crowned victors, heroes, and emperors as the ultimate symbol of glory.

symbolism.origin: Crowned ancient Olympic victors.

products.title: Lily of the Valley
products.description: Lily of the valley (Convallaria majalis) is a delicate woodland perennial producing arching stems of small, intensely fragrant, bell-shaped white flowers in spring. It is one of the most beloved of all spring flowers.

symbolism.origin: Legend of St. Leonard defeating a dragon.

products.title: Magnolia
products.description: Magnolias are ancient flowering trees and shrubs producing spectacular, goblet or star-shaped flowers in white, pink, purple, and yellow before the leaves emerge in spring. Among the earliest flowering plants on Earth.

symbolism.origin: Tall, enduring trees symbolized nobility.

products.title: Mistletoe
products.description: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant that grows as rounded clumps on tree branches, producing waxy white berries in winter. Sacred to the Druids and central to Norse mythology, it is the basis of the Christmas kissing custom.

symbolism.origin: Norse myth of Balder’s death and resurrection.

products.title: Monkshood
products.description: Monkshood (Aconitum), also called wolfsbane, is a tall perennial producing hooded flowers in deep blue or purple on arching spikes. Beautiful but highly toxic, it was historically used as a poison in warfare and hunting.

symbolism.origin: Petals resemble a knight’s helmet.

products.title: Myrtle
products.description: Myrtle (Myrtus communis) is a fragrant Mediterranean evergreen shrub with small, glossy leaves and white flowers followed by blue-black berries. Sacred to Aphrodite and Venus, it has been used in wedding ceremonies since antiquity.

symbolism.origin: Sacred to Aphrodite and used in weddings.

products.title: Nettle
products.description: Stinging nettles are vigorous perennials with deeply toothed, dark green leaves covered in hollow stinging hairs. Despite their sting, nettles are highly nutritious, have many medicinal uses, and are vital habitat for butterfly larvae.

symbolism.origin: From the painful stings and Andersen’s fairy tale.

products.title: Oak
products.description: Oak trees are majestic, long-lived deciduous or evergreen trees producing acorns, the classic fruit of the forest. Sacred to the thunder gods of multiple cultures, the oak is a symbol of strength, endurance, and bravery.

symbolism.origin: Sacred tree in Greek, Norse, and Celtic cultures.

products.title: Oleander
products.description: Oleander (Nerium oleander) is a beautiful, fast-growing Mediterranean shrub producing clusters of fragrant flowers in shades of pink, red, and white throughout summer. Highly ornamental but extremely toxic in all its parts.

symbolism.origin: Poisonous plant linked to tragic Greek myth.

products.title: Olive
products.description: The olive tree is one of humanity's oldest cultivated plants, native to the Mediterranean, producing the fruits from which olive oil is pressed. With gnarled silver-leaved beauty and longevity spanning millennia, it is a symbol of peace.

symbolism.origin: Biblical story of Noah’s dove.

products.title: Orange Blossom
products.description: Orange blossoms are the intensely fragrant white flowers of the orange tree (Citrus sinensis). Used in bridal wreaths and as the source of neroli essential oil and orange blossom water, they are among the world's most prized floral scents.

symbolism.origin: Popularized by Queen Victoria’s wedding.

products.title: Orchid
products.description: Orchids are one of the largest and most diverse families of flowering plants, with over 25,000 species worldwide. Prized for their extraordinarily beautiful and complex flowers, they have been symbols of luxury and elegance since the Victorian era.

symbolism.origin: Rare luxury flower in the Victorian era.

products.title: Passionflower
products.description: Passionflowers (Passiflora) are exotic climbing vines producing extraordinarily complex, alien-looking flowers with elaborate fringed coronas. Native to the Americas, the flowers and their symbolic parts were interpreted by Jesuits as symbols of the Passion of Christ.

symbolism.origin: Jesuits interpreted it as a symbol of Christ’s Passion.

products.title: Petunia
products.description: Petunias are among the most popular summer bedding plants, producing masses of trumpet-shaped flowers in every color of the rainbow throughout the season. Available in trailing and upright forms, they are superb in containers.

symbolism.origin: Delicate nature likened to wounded emotions.

products.title: Poppy
products.description: Poppies produce large, tissue-paper-thin flowers in shades of red, orange, pink, purple, and white. The red poppy is a universal symbol of remembrance for fallen soldiers, while the opium poppy has been cultivated for millennia for its latex.

symbolism.origin: Associated with opium and the land of the dead.

products.title: Protea
products.description: Proteas are dramatic South African flowering shrubs producing large, globe-shaped flower heads with striking cone-like centers. Among the most ancient of flowering plants, named for the shape-changing god Proteus for their extraordinary diversity.

symbolism.origin: Named after Proteus, the shape-shifting god.

products.title: Queen Anne’s Lace
products.description: Queen Anne's lace (Daucus carota) is a delicate wildflower and the wild ancestor of the cultivated carrot, producing flat-topped clusters of tiny white flowers with a single dark purple floret at the center.

symbolism.origin: Nest-like flower heads suggested shelter.

products.title: Rose
products.description: Roses are among the world's most beloved and cultivated flowers, with a history spanning 35 million years. Symbolizing love, beauty, and passion, they are grown in thousands of varieties worldwide and are central to perfumery, medicine, and art.

symbolism.origin: Long-standing symbol of love in myth and culture.

products.title: Rosemary
products.description: Rosemary (Salvia rosmarinus) is an aromatic Mediterranean shrub with needle-like silvery-green leaves and small blue flowers. A versatile culinary and medicinal herb, it has been associated with memory and remembrance since antiquity.

symbolism.origin: Greek scholars wore it to aid memory.

products.title: Rue
products.description: Rue (Ruta graveolens) is a pungent, bitter evergreen herb with blue-green, deeply divided leaves and small yellow flowers. Used medicinally since antiquity, it is associated with regret and was strewn in medieval courts to ward off disease.

symbolism.origin: Victorians used its bitterness as a warning.

products.title: Snapdragon
products.description: Snapdragons (Antirrhinum majus) are classic cottage garden annuals producing tall spikes of distinctive two-lipped flowers in a wide range of colors. Beloved by children for the snapping action of the hinged blooms when squeezed.

symbolism.origin: Worn by women to discourage unwanted advances.

products.title: Snowdrop
products.description: Snowdrops (Galanthus) are among the earliest flowers of the year, pushing through frozen ground in late winter to reveal their nodding, white bell-shaped flowers. A symbol of hope, they signal the end of winter.

symbolism.origin: Blooms in winter, signaling spring’s return.

products.title: Sweet Pea
products.description: Sweet peas (Lathyrus odoratus) are annual climbing plants producing clusters of frilly, intensely fragrant flowers in shades of pink, mauve, red, blue, white, and bicolors. Among the most fragrant of all garden flowers.

symbolism.origin: Victorian hostess gift.
meanings: Thank you for a lovely time

products.title: Tansy
products.description: Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare) is a vigorous, aromatic perennial with finely divided fern-like leaves and clusters of small, bright yellow button flowers. Historically used as an insect repellent, in cooking, and in herbal medicine.

symbolism.origin: Caused illness when misused medicinally.

products.title: Thistle
products.description: Thistles are robust, spiny plants producing purple or pink pom-pom flower heads beloved by goldfinches and bees. The thistle is the national emblem of Scotland, associated with the legend of a Viking invader who cried out on stepping on one.

symbolism.origin: Biblical and physical prickliness symbolism.

products.title: Violet
products.description: Violets (Viola odorata) are low-growing perennials producing heart-shaped leaves and dainty, sweetly fragrant flowers in deep violet, pale mauve, or white in early spring. The flowers are edible and have been used in perfumery.

symbolism.origin: Low-growing posture symbolized humility.

products.title: Wheat
products.description: Wheat (Triticum) is one of the world's most important cereal crops, with tall stalks bearing heavy heads of grain. As a symbol of fertility and harvest, sheaves of wheat have appeared in religious and cultural ceremonies since Neolithic times.

symbolism.origin: Ancient symbol of prosperity and harvest.

products.title: Willow
products.description: Willow trees are graceful, moisture-loving trees with long, narrow leaves and distinctive catkins. The weeping willow, with its sweeping, trailing branches, is a classic symbol of mourning and melancholy in literature and art.

symbolism.origin: Drooping branches associated with grief.

products.title: Wormwood
products.description: Wormwood (Artemisia absinthium) is a silvery-grey aromatic perennial herb with deeply divided leaves and small yellow flower heads. The source of absinthe's distinctive flavor, it has been used medicinally since ancient times.

symbolism.origin: Biblical references to suffering and sorrow.

products.title: Yarrow
products.description: Yarrow (Achillea millefolium) is a robust perennial wildflower with feathery aromatic leaves and flat-topped clusters of tiny flowers in white, yellow, pink, or red. Named after Achilles, who is said to have used it to heal wounds.

symbolism.origin: Named after Achilles, who healed wounds with it.

products.title: Primrose
products.description: Primroses (Primula) are charming spring-flowering perennials producing clusters of bright, cheerful blooms in shades of yellow, red, pink, purple, and white. They thrive in cool, moist soil and partial shade.

symbolism.origin: Among the first flowers to bloom in spring, symbolizing youth and new beginnings.

products.title: Viola
products.description: Violas are delicate, cheerful perennials or annuals producing small, sweetly scented flowers in shades of purple, blue, yellow, and white. More cold-hardy than pansies, they bloom prolifically from spring through early summer.

symbolism.origin: In Renaissance art, depicted as a symbol of faithfulness and modesty.

products.title: Butterfly Weed
products.description: Butterfly weed (Asclepias tuberosa) is a bright North American wildflower producing dense clusters of vibrant orange, yellow, or red flowers. A critical host plant for monarch butterfly caterpillars, it is essential for pollinator gardens.

symbolism.origin: Vital role in butterfly life cycles symbolizes transformation and resilience.

products.title: Celosia
products.description: Celosia, or cockscomb, is a vibrant annual producing velvety, brain-like flower heads in shades of red, pink, purple, yellow, and orange. The exotic appearance belies its ease of cultivation and heat tolerance.

symbolism.origin: The crested flowers resemble a rooster's comb, symbolizing boldness and confidence.

products.title: Centaurea
products.description: Centaurea (bachelor's button, cornflower) produces delicate, fringed flowers in shades of blue, purple, pink, and white. Easy to grow from seed and attractive to pollinators, they are a staple of cottage gardens.

symbolism.origin: Named for the centaur of Greek mythology; its bright color symbolized clarity.

products.title: Cosmos
products.description: Cosmos are graceful annuals producing delicate, daisy-like flowers on airy stems in shades of pink, red, orange, purple, and white. Heat and drought tolerant, they bloom prolifically from summer until frost.

symbolism.origin: The name means 'harmony' and 'order' from the Greek, reflecting its perfect symmetry.
